directions: Plant after last frost in rich, well-drained soil in a site ranging from full sun to fairly deep shade, or grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light; Electric Flash cordyline is notably heat tolerant and holds its chocolate-and-white variegation across a wider light range than most ti plants. Strap-shaped leaves emerge chocolate-bronze and mature to a dramatic variegated pattern splashed with cream, white, and pink over a deep green base, borne on an upright, cane-like stem typical of forest cabbage trees. A patented selection of Cordyline banksii (sold under the trade name Electric Flash, cultivar name 'Sprilecflash'), it is native to New Zealand and prized in Gulf Coast landscapes as a bold accent shrub or large container specimen. Water when the top inch of soil dries, protect from frost outside zones 9-11, and avoid overly wet, poorly drained soil, which can cause root rot.
